policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv נביאה and qere נביא are alternative spellings of the singular emphatic 'the prophet'; ASV 'Haggai the prophet' renders either identically and the only note is an alternative_rendering on a different phrase. Base qere carries the projection.

Ketiv נביאיא and qere נבייא are orthographic variants of the plural emphatic 'the prophets'; ASV 'Now the prophets' does not distinguish them and the alternative_rendering note concerns 'in the name of', not this word. Base qere carries the projection.

Ketiv נביאיא and qere נבייא are spelling variants of the plural emphatic 'the prophets'; ASV 'the prophets of God' renders either the same way and no note is mapped to this verse. Base qere carries the projection.

ASV 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean' is singular, in apposition to the king; that renders the qere singular emphatic כסדאה. The ketiv כסדיא is plural emphatic 'the Chaldeans', which the English wording excludes. The alternative_rendering note concerns 'after that', not this word.
Ketiv אלה and qere אל are both the Aramaic plural demonstrative 'these'; ASV 'Take these vessels' renders either identically and no note is mapped to this verse. Base qere carries the projection.
